title: Let a CLI ls --json caller request a larger page byte budget
outcome: Let a CLI ls --json caller request a larger page byte budget
acceptance: An opt-in CLI option on `engram work ls` (e.g. `--page-bytes N`, valid only with --json, bounded to an explicit maximum such as 1 MiB) raises the per-page response byte budget, so `ls --all --verbose --json --limit 200` returns up to 200 rows per page; continuation anchoring on the last emitted row and the more/after semantics are unchanged.

Without the option, CLI and MCP output, the 12 KiB default budget and cursor behaviour are byte-for-byte unchanged; the MCP surface does not gain the option; out-of-range values are refused with an actionable message.

completion.summary: `engram work ls --json --page-bytes N` (12288..=1048576) fits each listing page to N bytes, so `ls --all --verbose --json --limit 200` returns full 200-row pages. Rows, order, last-emitted-row cursors and more/after are unchanged, and cursors continue across budgets. The option is refused without --json or out of range, with an actionable message. Without it the CLI runs the unchanged `ls`, and MCP `ls` gains no option. Landed as 17a28f2 after review rounds 1-6 (the last two clean), full gate test-97f28fd0 PASS on freeze d35e48a9, and independent evaluations ee746bc4 and 849229a9 PASS 2/2 (the second fresh after landing). Installed build c2ac63da (exe sha256 cc1cc903…a97557); the backup of 787a310a is engram-20261016T152339Z-787a310a5b24.exe. All five live stores are ready.
